implied_move_source: UNAVAILABLE - there is no functioning option market in LUXE. The full chain was retrieved from https://query2.finance.yahoo.com/v7/finance/options/LUXE on 2026-09-14: four expiries only (2026-09-18, 2026-10-16, 2026-12-18, 2027-03-19), a six-strike grid (2.5/5/7.5/10/15/17.5), bid = 0.00 on every contract in the first post-event expiry, 95 contracts of total open interest in that expiry, and the ATM $7.50 call last traded 2026-05-04. The only fresh print anywhere is the 2026-09-18 $7.50 put at $0.45, traded 2026-09-14, volume 1, open interest 0, no bid, no ask. Inverting that single print (S=7.44, K=7.50, T=4d, r=4.1%) gives ATM IV 135% and E|move| 11.3%; 2x that put as a straddle x0.85 gives 10.3%. Those converge with the historical-reaction proxy (10.44% eight-quarter mean abs, 12.76% six-quarter median abs), so the working anchor used in the dossier is ~11-12%, but a one-lot print with a zero bid is not a sourced implied move and this field is therefore null.

notes.direction_read_rationale: Modest positive tilt resting on positioning and mechanics, not on fundamentals, with magnitude conviction far higher than direction conviction. Long side: 3,959,681 shares short at 25-47 days to cover against a float that on the coherent estimate is ~17m shares, in a stock trading $782k/day with NO option market to hedge in and 30 Stocktwits messages since February; no run-up at all (-2.62% over 20 sessions while Richemont is -8.7% and LVMH -8.4%); a mechanical FX flip that should carry reported group growth from -5.2% toward flat-or-positive with no underlying improvement; the 700-person layoff's full effect landing in Q4; a strong Apr-Jun demand backdrop (Richemont +20% cc, LVMH F&LG's first rise in two years, Revolve +12% with July +18%); 0.72x book with 43% of market cap in cash and every one of five analyst targets above spot; and four of the last six prints up, two of them +21.09% and +23.80%. Short side: the event is FY27 guidance and the bar is pre-set by JPMorgan's EUR117m CY27 EBITDA (~4.6% margin) against an FY26 of ~-0.14%, with the CFO having already spent the good news at Goldman 48 hours earlier; three pre-flagged Q4 drags (higher marketing ratio, adj EBITDA only 'around Q3 levels', first full quarter of de minimis elimination at 250bp of Mytheresa's cost ratio); deteriorating growth quality (active customers -7.5% YoY, top customers >40% of revenue vs 25-30% at IPO); two of three segments still shrinking ex-FX; an ADVERSE KPMG ICFR opinion with YNAP's 69% of assets excluded, followed seven months ago by a share-count misstatement in an earnings press release; incoherent consensus; one EPS beat in four quarters; a luxury complex down 5-9% in twenty sessions; Richemont's lock-up expired and MYT Holding's registration right unexercised over ~47% of the register; and a last print of -11.81%. Net: +15 / 55%, Low-Med conviction. Sizing should respect a 12.76% six-quarter median absolute move, a 23.80% maximum, $782k of daily liquidity and no options to hedge in.
notes.what_flips_it: Not a bad quarter - a credible quantified FY27 guide into the most illiquid short book in the day's universe. FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin of 4%+ on high-single-digit-or-better ex-FX growth, with NAP/MRP explicitly guided to full-year positive adjusted EBITDA and the EUR4bn / 7-9% framework reaffirmed with a dated path, converts JPMorgan's EUR117m from a model input into company guidance - 8x that is its own $10 target, 34% above spot, on 0.72x book. The mirror image needs no bad quarter either: FY27 guided to ~1-2%, or the EUR4bn target pushed beyond FY29, or a second reporting error/restated comparative in the release itself. Three tells resolvable within minutes of 08:30 ET: (1) is FY27 adjusted EBITDA margin guided as a number or only as 'improving' - qualitative is itself the bear outcome; (2) does the release restate prior-year comparatives for THE OUTNET; (3) the open - gap and close have agreed in direction 8 of 8, but the session extended the gap in only 5 of 8 and the two fades were violent (-11.0% intraday on 2025-09-25).
